request: Review this display path in an audio plugin.
artifact: The callback writes ordinary f32 samples into a history array. The UI copies the array, then compares the producer cursor before and after the copy and discards changed frames.

request: Can this meter use relaxed atomics?
artifact: The callback atomically stores one f32 peak value. The UI atomically loads it. No pointer, timestamp, or ordinary payload accompanies the value.
The change says acquire and release always compile to the same instructions as relaxed loads and stores on ARM, so every queue operation can use relaxed ordering.
A full queue drops the newest event. A note-on may already be queued when its note-off cannot be queued.
The UI atomically swaps a prepared pointer. A bounded retirement queue is full, and the callback may still read the old object.
A TSan job passed, but the shared module was linked without instrumentation. Its deliberately weakened ordering control also passed.
The defective arm exits before the marked callback because the host fixture cannot load its bundle. The expected prohibited-operation diagnostic is absent.
RTSan detects allocation in a standalone executable. The host loads the plugin through dlopen and its render worker is not marked as a real-time context.
A Loom model replaces only the queue atomics. A dependency retains standard synchronization types, and exploration ends at a configured preemption bound.
A state loader receives a byte slice from a harness. The parser trusts declared lengths and may convert values before range checks.
Average CPU time is low, but the first callback after activation and a periodic cleanup both exceed the block interval.
The main thread decodes a truncated preset and swaps partially initialized state while process may run.
The plugin stores the operating-system thread ID from its first process call and rejects later process calls from a different thread.
The adapter assumes equal input and output channels, wraps aliased host pointers as independent mutable Rust slices, and fills only active output channels.
A JUCE processor assumes every block has the preparation size. A CLAP adapter copies an incoming block larger than its activated maximum into fixed scratch.
Reset clears a large preallocated delay line. Render workers share one scratch buffer and can publish to a channel described as SPSC.
A full bounded queue drops a reference-counted payload, whose final destructor posts a UI notification. Successful submissions also call an asynchronous notifier from process.
A new enum member shifts existing parameter numbers. The display labels are unchanged and no saved automation fixture is available.
CLAP parameters are [A, B, C]. The wrapper ordering is [2, 0, 1], and the review cites only a header that describes the mapping.
A preset changes latency and ports. The host delays restart after request_restart, while process reports the pending configuration as active.
The scheduler receives equal-offset notes, delayed notes, wildcard addresses, and a timeline discontinuity. It compares note_id only.
Audio is silent, but a delayed note and a rejected note-off remain pending. The processor returns CLAP_PROCESS_SLEEP.
A VST3 queue supplies only a final point for a block. An AUv3 ramp crosses three render blocks. The adapter starts a fresh smoother at each endpoint.
The processor adds a global CLAP modulation to a polyphonic modulation amount and runs multiplicative smoothing toward zero.
A recursive tail can enter the subnormal range. A finite input can overflow internal state, and the build uses floating-point optimization flags.
A supposedly host-independent core lives in a separate directory but can import the plugin SDK through a transitive package. No failing dependency control exists.
Core vectors pass. The adapter still has no tests for buffer aliases, event offsets, process status, or delayed restart notifications.
